origins.section: A Project's Cost Lands in the Years It Is Worked On
Build Spend as an Expression Once, and Every Budget Rule Reuses It
Charging Everything to the Start Year Breaks the Budget the Plan Claims to Respect

gates.says: all 3 of this quiz's answerable readings held and each was taken over the question as it stands

recorded.prompt:q-coefficient: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-coefficient: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-coefficient: "spend_y = sum_i sum_{t<=y} c_{i,y-t} x_{i,t}" with k counted from 0; for 2030, start 2028 -> k=2 -> 300, start 2029 -> k=1 -> 500 (cf. P022 example: 1470 x_2027 + 720 x_2028 + 360 x_2029).
recorded.prompt:q-reuse: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-reuse: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-reuse: "Writing the triple loop again in each place is how two parts of one model end up disagreeing about what a project costs in 2030. Nothing fails when the copies drift apart ... Each rule simply uses its own idea of spend."
recorded.prompt:q-lump: Read the whole lesson page, then this question. Using only what the page states, which option does the page decide is correct? Quote or cite the deciding passage.
recorded.pass:q-lump: page reader (independent agent; saw the lesson pages and the question)
recorded.outcome:q-lump: "The overrun lands at the end of the plan because that is where long projects started in earlier years keep spending. The lump model thinks that money was paid in the start year, so it fills those later years with new starts as well."

recorded.outcome:q-lump:d: "The budgets do not cause it either: the spread model meets the very same budgets in every year." The page spreads project costs, never budgets; the overrun is "spending the model never counted", not double counting.
